calls.head: Boston rolls four lines; Winnipeg leans on its top six
calls.body: Boston ranks 2nd of 32 for depth, toward the deep end; Winnipeg ranks 29th, toward the top-heavy end.
calls.call: Boston spreads its forward ice time deeper down the lineup than Winnipeg.

calls.happened: On bottom-six share of forward ice time, Boston had 44% and Winnipeg 43%. Coming in, Boston was at 44% and Winnipeg at 40%.

calls.head: Boston’s power play outclasses Winnipeg’s
calls.body: On power play, Boston sits 8th of 32, at the lethal end of the scale. Winnipeg is 28th, at the harmless end.
calls.call: Boston’s power play creates more per 60 than Winnipeg’s.

calls.happened: On power-play expected goals per 60, Boston had 3.8 per 60 and Winnipeg 19.2 per 60. Coming in, Boston was at 7.8 per 60 and Winnipeg at 7.0 per 60.

WPG.head: We had this close to even (55% for Winnipeg), and it went Boston’s way.

BOS.head: We had this close to even (45% for Boston), and Boston came through.

surprises.head: Winnipeg’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Winnipeg’s power play created 19.2 expected goals per 60, against its usual 7.0 and a league average of 7.5. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 100 games.

surprises.head: Winnipeg was kept to the outside
surprises.body: Winnipeg needed 21.5 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 16.6 and a league average of 15.9. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 7 games.
